src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2020_us_cd116_500k
cd.vint: The Census Bureau's lines of the 116th Congress's districts (its file says session 116). The Bureau published no file of the 117th Congress's districts, the Congress the 2020 election chose.
rec: 2018 remedial congressional plan, 18 districts, imposed by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court (League of Women Voters v. Commonwealth)
Supreme Court of Pennsylvania, League of Women Voters v. Commonwealth, No. 159 MM 2017, per curiam order of 2018-02-19 adopting the remedial congressional plan

The court struck the 2011 plan (Congressional Redistricting Act of 2011, 25 P.S. 3596.101 et seq.) on 2018-01-22 and adopted its own plan on 2018-02-19 for the 2018 primary; it was used in 2018 and 2020. The cd116 file (116th Congress) holds the 2018 lines; Pennsylvania lost a seat in the 2020 Census.

src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2020_us_sldu_500k
sldu.vint: The Census Bureau's 2020 file of legislative districts, the lines it records for the 2018 legislative session year. The Bureau published no file of the lines in use for 2020. Where a state's lines changed in between, the check below or the plan cited stops the map.
rec: 2012 Revised Final Reapportionment Plan, 50 Senate districts (Legislative Reapportionment Commission, adopted 2012-06-08)
Pennsylvania Legislative Reapportionment Commission: plans and maps (lists the '2012 Revised Final' and '2021 Final' plans for both chambers)

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court rejected the Commission's first plan (Holt v. 2011 LRC, 2012) and held the 2001 plan for the 2012 elections; it accepted the revised plan in 2013 (Holt v. 2011 LRC, 67 A.3d 1211), effective for the 2014 elections. 25 Senate seats were up in 2020. The 2020 file (LSY 2018) holds it.
